This document separates actual human decisions from the large body of model-generated specifications, audits, summaries, and proposed terminology produced during development.
A ruling in this ledger may:
- **Exact statement:** “These are the 4.7 docs before 0.5.0 Home Mode, Colony, and DWELL Specification, the first document of what I consider to be 0.5.”
- **Affected sources:** intended-v0.4.7 decisions; spatial review; Home Mode, Colony, and DWELL Specification; legacy concordance; future corpus manifest.

section: ## HR-LIN-001 — Home Mode, Colony, and DWELL Specification begins v0.5

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Yes they're there as old, but the intention of v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward and the BSA (covering different phases of the 0.4.7 docs, along with maybe even one more spec?) was to preserve their learnings so they (047 decisions) didn't contaminate further development with old ideas.”
- **Affected sources:** V6/V7 decisions; v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward; BSA audit and ledgers; descendant specifications.
- **Semantic scope:** corpus lineage and source disposition.

section: ## HR-LIN-002 — v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward and BSA as contamination barriers

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Lineagewise, the BSA returns from 0.4.7 as I read them resulted in several massive tangents resulting in dedicated 0.5 Spec Docs -- what's called BSA11 was a fifty round development of entire families of systems.”
- **Affected sources:** Personal Items specification; BSA-12–22 consolidation; BSA audit and disposition ledger; corpus manifest.
- **Semantic scope:** corpus lineage and document classification.

section: ## HR-LIN-003 — BSA branches may become dedicated systems

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “And add to the list please compare the two documents Philosophy Spec 0.5 & Philosophy Architecture and make one. The 0.5 Spec was made early about the difference between 0.4 and a nascent 0.5; the Architecture was made close to the end of the process, about the entire game overall.”
- **Affected sources:** early Philosophical Specification; Philosophical Architecture v2.0; `M050_Governing_Philosophy_and_Architecture_v1_0_MEDIANv0_5_0.md`.

section: ## HR-PHIL-001 — Merge the two philosophy generations

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Do this -- end-note it. Keep it out of the body of the ‘present tense’ philosophy doc, for purity, but make it avail of searches for.”
- **Affected sources:** merged philosophy document; compiler publication states.

section: ## HR-PHIL-002 — Philosophy history belongs in a silent endnote

members.text: - **Authority effect:** Prevents Pillars from being misclassified as structural components.
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; merged philosophy; future Semantic Registry.

section: ## HR-PHIL-003 — Philosophy and Architecture are distinct domains

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “a tweak on Philosophy.Principles.LegibilityPreceedArtachmenr is actually a late added Pillar. And it should have been GamelogicPreceedsAttachment which is the pillar that if the Player is worried about colony mechanics, they don't have the headspace to fully appreciate Attachment-forward aspects, so all Attachment-forward systems must have a gane mechanic aspect.”
- **Affected sources:** Governing Philosophy and Architecture; MSID Grammar; Embodiment; Sourcebook.

section: ## HR-PHIL-004 — Game Logic Precedes Attachment is the eighth Pillar

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Canonical Registers are Colony, Field, Crossing, Encounter, and Embodiment -- not Travel. TRAVEL is Field Register verb.”
- **Affected sources:** Governing Philosophy and Architecture; MSID Grammar; Away; v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward; reconciliation correction rules; future registry.

section: ## HR-ARCH-001 — The five Registers include Field, not Travel

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “the Body-Unit principle (basically Mouse has general numeric equivalency the other two with the individual 2x Citizen count) needs to be detailed somewhere in Phil or Arch and it's not as of now.”
- **Affected sources:** Governing Philosophy and Architecture; MSID Grammar; Core Species Traits; Away; Crossing; Population; future registry.

section: ## HR-ARCH-002 — Body Unit is MEDIAN's cross-species equivalency scale

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “I want to adopt a new file nomenclature with M050_ as the prefix followed by the content heavy name part of the name at the front, for ease of iPhone reading, and MEDIANv0_5_0 at the end. This will also help keep files clear from pre canon redo.”
- **Authority effect:** Establishes the naming convention for canon-redo artifacts.
- **Affected sources:** all new M050 files; future corpus manifest.
- **Semantic scope:** file and build process only.
- **Exact statement:** “Then we use those new names forever onward.”
- **Affected sources:** source-identity and reconciliation manifest v0.2; File Nomenclature Migration Ledger; repository links, indexes, scripts, and future documents.
- **Semantic scope:** file and build process only.

section: ## HR-FILE-002 — Canonical M050 filenames become the permanent current names

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “HR-CROSS-001 is wrong. Crossing is a Register, one of five. Its verb is RISK. It's SID is Away.Crossing, and it contains such systems as Away.Crossing.Phase and also Away.Crossing.Rabbit and Away.Crossing.Squirrel because Crossing is forked by Core Species in a way no other Regusters are.”
- **Affected sources:** Away; Crossing specification; provisional namespace; legacy concordance; MSID Grammar; merged philosophy's Register table.

section: ## HR-CROSS-001 — Crossing is a Register; RISK is its operator

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Body unit is three as a standard and maximum with an allowable exception of two body units, primarily to be untilized in early game when population is quite low.”
- **Affected sources:** Crossing; Core Species Traits; Away; BSA disposition records; Crossing Atomic Extraction Pilot; Governing Philosophy and Architecture.

section: ## HR-AWAY-003 — Ordinary expeditions use three Body Units with a two-unit early-game exception

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Two distinct things. ‘Gathering Place’ (old Story Circle; Circle too rabbity) is a Practice for Teacher Role, and provides diegetic access to the Chronicle, displayed through a View pane.”
- **Affected sources:** Home; v0.4.6 GDD Coverage-Gap Development; legacy concordance; future Semantic Registry.
- **Semantic scope:** `Home.Colony.Practice.GatheringPlace`; `Home.Colony.Role.Teacher`; Chronicle/View branch pending final path.

section: ## HR-HOME-001 — Gathering Place, Teacher, and Chronicle are distinct units

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “‘Place of Pride’ lets deprecate as a concept for now.”
- **Affected sources:** Home; BSA ledgers; v0.4.6 GDD Coverage-Gap Development; legacy concordance; provisional namespace.
- **Semantic scope:** Home display and civic-memory concepts.

- **Exact statement:** “OPEN-HOME-001 - the Community Board is an example of the third kind of Practice associated with Leadership. It's the diegetic source for Almanac material (current game & conditions) mirroring the Gathering Place as a diegetic source for Chronicle (history).”
- **Affected sources:** Home; v0.4.6 GDD Coverage-Gap Development; legacy concordance; MSID Grammar; future Semantic Registry and Sourcebook.
- **Semantic scope:** `Home.Colony.Practice.CommunityBoard`; Leadership branch pending exact MSID; Almanac and Chronicle branches pending exact MSIDs.

section: ## HR-HOME-003 — Community Board is the Leadership Practice for the Almanac

members.text: - **Affected sources:** v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward; Away; BSA memory rulings; merged philosophy; legacy concordance.

section: ## HR-MEM-001 — Distinctions and After-names follow meaningful history

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Full keep and conform fully to Hyphen bound orthography for animal-related concepts which would be ‘one word’ in the squirrel language, explicitly modeled after the theory on Tolkien, explained in an appendix.”
- **Affected sources:** Appendix Architecture; Semantic Registry; naming banks; all M050 prose.
- **Semantic scope:** language, names, and canonical display forms.

section: ## HR-LANG-001 — Hyphen-bound animal-cultural compounds are canonical

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “I want to add an explicit prose style guide.”
- **Affected sources:** Authorial Grammar; MSID Grammar; source-identity and reconciliation manifest v0.2; Sourcebook; Phonebook.
- **Semantic scope:** authorial process and prose presentation.

section: ## HR-LANG-002 — MEDIAN uses a standalone Authorial Grammar

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Significant nouns in the game have initial caps, experiential VERBS are all caps, MSID is Thing.Thing dot separated.”
- **Affected sources:** all active specifications; Sourcebook; Phonebook; future authoring lint.

section: ## HR-LANG-003 — Defined Terms use Initial Caps; experiential operators use ALL CAPS

members.text: - “Species can be referred to by nonplairalized forms ex ‘Mouse builds a Manor House’ means as ‘The Mouse core species builds Manor Houses’.”
- “Squirrel connects a separated Place” and “Squirrels connect separated Places.” Both are valid.
- “My mistake -- that should have been ‘builds’ present tense in the Mouse sentence.”
- **Affected sources:** Authorial Grammar; Ecology; P&A species doctrine; Home; Away; Sourcebook captions and prose.

section: ## HR-LANG-004 — Bare Core-Species Singular is permitted

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “‘Prior-life Tale’ needs a lower case L in life. This is lifted directly from Lord of the Rings as a two-word hyphenated compound with the first word Capitalized and the second word not.”
- **Authority effect:** Clarifies the canonical internal casing of Hyphen-bound compounds.
- **Affected sources:** Authorial Grammar; MSID Grammar; Chronicle and Tale materials; Sourcebook and Phonebook.
- **Semantic scope:** canonical names and display orthography.

section: ## HR-LANG-005 — Hyphen-bound internal elements remain lowercase

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “This can develop if more emergent grammar comes to light later (for example mechanics-teaching Narrative snippets are italicized).”
- **Affected sources:** Authorial Grammar; Sourcebook authoring; Narrative presentation; Phonebook.

section: ## HR-LANG-006 — Authorial grammar may emerge through repeated practice

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “this will guide our authoring process and then could be a single plate appendix in the Phoneboox appendixes”
- **Affected sources:** Authorial Grammar; Appendix Architecture; Phonebook.

section: ## HR-LANG-007 — The Phonebook receives a derived grammar plate

members.text: - **Affected sources:** v0.4.6 GDD Coverage-Gap Development; Away; v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward; legacy concordance; future corpus manifest.

section: ## HR-AWAY-001 — Latest Outpost work has scoped authority

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “The current ‘Muted DWELL’ look and Away.Encounter.Stopover (a lesser version version of Home.Encounter.Homecoming).”
- **Authority effect:** Settles the mode/presentation distinction and current Stopover identity.
- **Affected sources:** v0.4.6 GDD Coverage-Gap Development; Away; v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward; MSID Grammar; future Sourcebook.

section: ## HR-AWAY-002 — Stopover remains Away with Muted DWELL presentation

members.text: - **Authority effect:** Constrains source authority while permitting scoped promotions.
- **Affected sources:** v0.4.6 GDD Coverage-Gap Development; future source-identity and reconciliation manifest.

section: ## HR-AUTH-001 — v0.4.6 GDD Coverage-Gap Development is supplementary outside promoted scopes

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Yes that's good. Ecology was a layer I didn't fully engage with because I was afraid of letting its biological-strict considerations get into the spec without rogorous evaluation. I think we include as a subsidiary document.”
- **Affected sources:** Ecological Influences; source-identity and reconciliation manifest; Home; Away; Crossing; Embodiment; Core Species Traits.
- **Semantic scope:** ecological translation and source authority.

section: ## HR-AUTH-002 — Ecology is an active subsidiary owner, not an unattended biological authority

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Yes the semantic unit is a property of the game, NOT the book.”
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; Sourcebook architecture; extraction pipeline; Semantic Registry.

section: ## HR-SEM-001 — Semantic Units belong to MEDIAN

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Verb doesn't enter the namespace. The namespace name is Home.Colony.Practice.Garden, and it's staffed by a Home.Colony.Role.Gardener. All of this happens ‘in DWELL’. In Crossing, it's ‘Away.Crossing.Phase.Observe’ and the act that describes is one of RISK.”
- **Affected sources:** provisional namespace; atomic extraction schema; MSID Grammar.

section: ## HR-SEM-002 — Namespace paths identify ontology, not operators

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “And this Semantic ID scheme will be such an understanding aid -- it tells the reader EXACTLY how to contextualize what they're currently reading.”
- **Authority effect:** Creates a reader-comprehension acceptance test for the ontology.
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; Sourcebook; future Semantic Registry.

section: ## HR-SEM-003 — MSIDs are reader-facing contextual notation

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “It alone justifies our rigid hierarchical architecture.”
- **Authority effect:** Establishes a burden of proof for hierarchy depth and new branches.
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; ontology extraction; Sourcebook design.
- **Semantic scope:** architecture of the semantic registry.

section: ## HR-SEM-004 — Hierarchical rigor is justified by explanatory value

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “This is not quite right -- this should be Architecture.Register.Colony and .Embody (in noun form, not all capped as a verb. Also Embody probably needs a better Noun or VERB).”
- **Authority effect:** Corrects operator-shaped Register paths and closes the Embodiment naming question.
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; merged philosophy; future Semantic Registry.

section: ## HR-SEM-005 — Register MSIDs use nouns; Embodiment pairs with EMBODY

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “With the understanding by the judgement parsing brain that in devo I had no discipline with the term and mixed them up badly.”
- **Affected sources:** all pre-cleaned specifications; atomic extraction pipeline; MSID Grammar.

section: ## HR-SEM-006 — Historical source terminology is not trusted ontology

members.text: - **Authority effect:** Establishes two primary ontology branches and the location of Conservation of Systems.
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; merged philosophy; future Semantic Registry.
- **Exact statement:** “For me it was mainly to avoid one word TLD. I don't understand Home as necessarily a SID but Home.Home is explicitly so.”
- **Closing statement:** “Drop the convention below TLD so Home.Home stays but Home.Colony.Colony loses the dupe?”
- **Authority effect:** Establishes the Minimum Two-Segment Rule, TLD self-rooting, and branch-as-unit behavior.
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; future Semantic Registry; extraction validators.

section: ## HR-SEM-008 — TLDs are containers; root concepts self-root once

members.text: - **Exact question:** “should the Grammar to include a terminal entry that's one single distinct instance, ie Home.Colony.Role.Gardener.Bramble#R002”
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; extraction schema; future Entity ID Grammar.

section: ## HR-SEM-009 — Runtime instances are not terminal MSID segments

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “Added just now: Semantic ID abbreviated as MSID (Median Semantic Identifier) (it's a short word that's more unique than SID)”
- **Authority effect:** Renames the project-specific identifier notation and its short form.
- **Affected sources:** MSID Grammar; Human Rulings Ledger; compiler fields; Sourcebook; Semantic Registry.

section: ## HR-SEM-010 — MEDIAN Semantic Identifier is abbreviated MSID

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “These will likely be literal Sourcebook section index ids, at each section.”
- **Later correction:** “Yes the semantic unit is a property of the game, NOT the book.”
- **Authority effect:** Establishes the relation between ontology and page design.
- **Semantic scope:** publication use of all semantic units.

section: ## HR-SB-001 — Core sections display the unit's MSID

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “The main book presents all of the stuff, but at a tighter, more core level, and each core book section heading is ‘GARDENERS - Home.Colony.Role.Gardeners’, and then in ‘Part 2: the Phonebook Appendixes’ sections are ID'd by their namespace name.”
- **Affected sources:** Appendix Architecture; Sourcebook TOC; Semantic Registry.

section: ## HR-SB-002 — Dual-depth Sourcebook and Phonebook Appendixes

members.text: - **Exact statement:** “I actually think this opens up a massive Sourcebook organization opportunity ... with some of the more in-the-weeds and also back-end processes (like Jostle) ... explained in mechanical (eventually tuned) detail.”
- **Affected sources:** Sourcebook architecture; appendix plan; compiler cross-reference system.

section: ## HR-SB-003 — Part I and Part II are views of one rule
## OPEN-SEM-002 — Narrative as a Top-Level Domain

members.text: - **Do not infer:** The illustrative form `Citizen#R002` is not yet a frozen identifier standard.
